memoryText: For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Ephesians 2:8-9 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
These two verses may be the most quoted summary of the gospel of grace.

“For by grace.” Grace is God’s favor given freely to those who do not deserve it. It is the source of everything.

“You have been saved.” The verb is in the perfect tense: it was done in the past with results that continue. You are not hoping to be saved by your effort; you have been saved.

“Through faith.” Faith is the means by which we receive what grace offers. It is not a work but an empty hand. It looks to Christ.

“And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” Everything, including the faith itself, is God’s gift. We did not contribute.

“Not a result of works, so that no one may boast.” If salvation depended on us even a little, we could take some credit. As it is, all the glory goes to God.

And verse 10 adds what follows: we are his workmanship, created for good works. We are saved by grace, not by works, but for works.

When pride or despair threatens, say these verses. Both are answered by grace.
weekInReview: This week you began the Prison Epistles with Ephesians. In chapter 1, Paul praised God for blessing us in Christ with every spiritual blessing: chosen, adopted, redeemed, and sealed with the Spirit, to the praise of his glorious grace. Two doctrinal pauses considered election and predestination, and the nature of the church as the people of God built on Christ the cornerstone. Ephesians 2 and 3 showed us dead in sin and made alive by grace through faith, Jew and Gentile made one new humanity, and the mystery of Christ revealed. Chapters 4 to 6 turned to life in Christ: unity of the Spirit, gifts for equipping the saints, putting off the old self and putting on the new, walking in love, the household, and the armor of God.
reflectionQuestions: Paul says every spiritual blessing is ours in Christ. Which of the blessings in Ephesians 1:3-14 is hardest for you to believe is true of you? How might you remind yourself of it this week?
Ephesians 2:8-10 says we are saved by grace through faith, for good works. Which is your greater temptation: to rely on your works or to neglect them? How does grace answer both?
Ephesians 4 tells us to maintain the unity of the Spirit. Is there a relationship in your church or family where you need to take the first step? What is it?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that you are saved by grace through faith, a gift.
Rest in what Christ has done.
Ask him to keep you standing.
